blocks: JavaScript looks like Java and behaves differently. These differences cause most of the bugs Java developers write in it.

sections.title: Modern syntax you will read every day

blocks.title: Gotcha
blocks.text: `||` falls back on any falsy value, including `0` and `''`. `count || 10` gives 10 when count is 0; `count ?? 10` gives 0. Falsy values are `false`, `0`, `''`, `null`, `undefined` and `NaN`.

sections.title: Closures and this
blocks: A **closure** is a function that keeps access to the variables of the scope that created it, even after that scope has returned. React hooks depend on this completely.

blocks.title: A closure

walkthrough.title: Captured

walkthrough.title: State without a class
walkthrough.text: Each call updates the same captured `n`.

blocks: `this` is decided by **how a function is called**, not where it is defined. Arrow functions have no `this` of their own and use the enclosing one, which is why callbacks use them.

sections.title: The event loop, promises and async/await
blocks: The page has one thread. Slow work (network, timers) happens outside it and queues a callback for later. If your code blocks that thread, the page freezes: no clicks, no scrolling.

blocks.title: The event loop

blocks.caption: When the stack is empty, all microtasks run, then one task, then the browser may repaint.

blocks.title: The classic ordering question
async and await
Gotcha
blocks.text: `fetch` only rejects on network failure. A 404 or 500 resolves normally, so always check `res.ok`.

blocks.title: Interview angle
blocks.text: **Explain the event loop.** JavaScript runs on one thread with a call stack. Async operations run in the browser and queue callbacks. When the stack empties, the loop runs all microtasks (promise callbacks), then one task (timer, event), and the browser can repaint. This is why long synchronous work freezes the page.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Use `const` by default, `let` when needed, never `var`.
- Use `===`, never `==`.
- Closures keep access to their creating scope; hooks rely on them.
- Microtasks run before the next task.
- `fetch` resolves on HTTP errors: check `res.ok`.

items.question: What does `[] == false` give, and what should you do about it?
items.answer: `true`, through type coercion. Always use `===`, which never coerces.

items.question: What is the output order of `setTimeout(f, 0)` and `Promise.resolve().then(g)`?
items.answer: `g` then `f`: promise callbacks are microtasks, which run before the next task.

items.question: Why does `count || 10` misbehave when count is 0?
items.answer: `||` treats 0 as falsy and returns 10. Use `??`, which only falls back on null or undefined.

items.question: How do you run two requests in parallel and wait for both?
items.answer: `await Promise.all([a(), b()])`. It rejects as soon as either rejects; use `Promise.allSettled` to get every outcome.
